title: Maya Angelou: Caged Bird Voice
dek: The poet who turned years of silence into a public language of survival.
mortality_event: Childhood trauma and years of mutism before literature, mentorship, memoir, and civil-rights witness returned her voice to the world.
citation_passage: Maya Angelou (1928–2014) was an American writer, performer, and civil-rights activist whose autobiographical work brought personal experience into public literature. Childhood sexual violence was followed by years in which she did not speak; reading and poetry remained part of her life. Her memoir I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings recounts her early years, including trauma and racism. Angelou also worked as a singer and dancer, served the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, wrote poetry and essays, and taught at Wake Forest University. This seven-page biographical comic follows the relationship between silence, language, and the wider creative and public work through which she became known.
